overview.text: The Church’s June 30 gathering of the Twelve follows the June 29 commemoration of Peter and Paul. Individual apostles also have their own observances.
overview.reason: Necessary concise source-bound explanation;substantial modern text is not established as freely reproducible. This is an AI-written summary,not the source author’s wording.

blocks.text: The early-fourteenth-century Constantinopolitan panel gathers twelve haloed apostles into a close group. Books and scrolls mark the figures within a shared gold field. The file identifies the Pushkin Museum work as the Synaxis of the Twelve; the catalogue is not a key for replacing every painted figure with a name from a different narrative list.

blocks.text: The OCA connects the common feast with early observance and Constantine’s church of the Twelve Apostles at Constantinople. It points to Matthew10, Mark3, Luke6 and Acts1 for different biblical lists. Its commemorative list includes Matthias.

blocks.text:
And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.

Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;

Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;

Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not:

But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.

Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give.
blocks.context: The Gospel’s earlier commissioning list includes Judas Iscariot. It is quoted as canonical Scripture in its own narrative setting,not as the later feast’s roster or a named key to each painted face.
